section.name: preparation_overview
section.title: Before measurement: plan and prepare
section.help: Experiment Planner simulates a proposed POWGEN measurement from structures, instrument configuration, sample assumptions and exposure. Experiment preparation builds reusable magnetic responses and structural model libraries, generates examples and trains a ranking model. Save plans and libraries to History and carry reviewed inputs into analysis. Measured scans are not required for these preparation workflows.

section.name: experiment_overview
section.title: 1. Start with your IPTS
section.help: Connect to the SNS or HFIR experiment data available in NDIP. Find recorded samples, run numbers, reduced patterns and measurement conditions. Resolve supported instrument profiles or review the required bank/profile choice. Use chat to prepare the analysis configuration and choose a built-in or custom CIF library.

section.name: analysis_overview
section.title: 2. Analyze the scans and follow what changes
section.help: Run preliminary Rietveld analysis across selected scans and new arrivals: identify candidate crystalline phases and refine phase contributions, background and lattice parameters. Plot fractions and cell changes against temperature, time or other available conditions. Explore linked diffraction maps and optional ML-assisted feature suggestions for peaks appearing, disappearing, splitting or changing shape.

section.name: advanced_overview
section.title: 3. Refine further and explore structural or magnetic models
section.help: Describe a custom GSAS-II refinement through chat, review its stages and apply it across the series. Search commensurate magnetic k-vector candidates and compare compatible subgroups; generate and refine supported structural distortion models. For POWGEN, inspect WebMON snapshots and update reviewed, fixed-reference magnetic fits while data are collected.

tool.help:
Open the RADAR-PD workspace ===========================
Click **Run Tool** to start the interactive application. Select your experiment, data and analysis settings inside RADAR-PD. You can also analyze an uploaded pattern or reopen saved work.
What you can do ===============
* **Plan a measurement.** Preview POWGEN patterns, sample and isotope choices, structural or magnetic changes, exposure and conditional counting noise. Matched 2026B configurations support count predictions; unmatched profiles provide shape previews. Save the plan and its inputs to Galaxy History. * **Prepare reusable calculations.** Supply a nuclear CIF and bank profiles, select a commensurate scope, and prepare magnetic responses or structural candidates and training examples before beamtime. A trained ranking model prioritizes native comparisons; it does not prove a unique structure. * **Find an experiment from its IPTS.** Discover samples and scans from the facility data mounted in NDIP, read recorded conditions, and review the instrument setup. POWGEN supports automatic profile matching for registered configurations. Other cases may require a supplied profile and bank mapping. * **Configure the analysis through chat.** Select samples, scans, banks, structures and analysis settings, then check the inputs or test one scan. * **Run preliminary Rietveld analysis.** Search the selected CIF library and refine a multiphase model with phase contributions, background and cell parameters. Inspect each scan's fit, residuals and Bragg ticks. * **Follow an experimental series.** Process existing scans or monitor new reduced scans while the session is running. Plot phase fractions, lattice parameters, relative expansion, ratios and other supported derived quantities against qualified acquisition conditions. * **Locate diffraction changes.** Use linked timelines, intensity maps and optional, experimental ML-assisted local feature review to inspect peak emergence, disappearance, splitting, broadening and intensity changes. * **Request custom GSAS-II refinements.** Describe supported parameter releases, constraints and stages in plain language. Review the recipe, apply it to compatible scans and compare the new GPXs with the original results. * **Explore magnetic and structural hypotheses.** Screen commensurate k vectors, obtain compatible magnetic subgroups from Bilbao, or generate supported displacement-mode candidates with ISODISTORT. Run selected models with multiple starts and inspect the alternatives. These are bounded research comparisons, not guaranteed unique structure solutions. * **Inspect an acquisition in progress.** The POWGEN Live acquisition workspace reads WebMON reduced snapshots, shows the evolving pattern and supports conditional magnetic fitting against a reviewed nuclear reference. It does not currently recommend when to stop counting. * **Save and continue.** Preserve configurations, results and recovery records in Galaxy; download scientific outputs or open verified GPXs in hosted GSAS-II.
Access and getting started ==========================
POWGEN and NOMAD Live workflows are available. HB-2A and SNAP retain preview status. Available data depend on facility authorization and storage access.
LLM-assisted refinement requires Illumine access. Online magnetic subgroup discovery requires Bilbao access. If the site provides shared service access, no personal credential group is needed. Otherwise, select your optional credential groups in this form before starting a new session. Shared defaults are configured by NDIP administrators. Standard phase analysis does not require either service.
Use **User guide** inside the application for screenshots and example configurations. The analysis uses reduced diffraction data; its interpretation depends on the chosen candidate structures, calibration and fit quality.
Submitted scientific jobs and published History outputs remain in Galaxy when an interactive session ends.
